sentence: The NHS says insomnia usually improves by changing sleeping habits, and that a GP can arrange CBT when habits alone do not help.
note: NHS insomnia page: usually gets better by changing habits; GP may refer for CBT

sentence: The NHS describes insomnia as regular difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep or waking too early.
note: NHS: if you regularly find it hard to fall asleep, stay asleep or wake up too early you may have insomnia

sentence: A steady bedtime and wake time, a dark, quiet room and winding down without screens are the habits the NHS pages describe most often.
note: Every Mind Matters: regular routine, avoid phones an hour before bed, dark quiet cool room

sentence: The NHS suggests seeing a GP if changing habits has not helped, or if sleep trouble has lasted for months.
note: NHS: see a GP if habits have not helped or trouble sleeping for months

sentence: Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia is the main treatment described by NHS sources; sleeping pills are rarely prescribed.
note: NHS: GPs rarely prescribe sleeping pills; UCLH: most patients offered CBT-I first line

sentence: The NHS says a person who regularly finds it hard to fall asleep, stay asleep or wake up too early may have insomnia.
note: NHS insomnia: regularly find it hard to fall asleep, stay asleep, or wake up too early

sentence: It also says insomnia usually gets better by changing sleeping habits.
note: NHS insomnia: usually gets better by changing your sleeping habits

sentence: A primary care pathway from NHS South Yorkshire says insomnia often starts with a specific problem or a change in life circumstances.
note: South Yorkshire pathway: insomnia often starts with a specific problem or changes in life that should be explored

sentence: The same pathway lists physical conditions such as sleep apnoea as able to make insomnia worse.
note: South Yorkshire pathway flags physical conditions such as sleep apnoea that can worsen it

sentence: It also suggests that a clinician asks whether a medicine could be a cause, and considers anxiety or depression as possible underlying factors.
note: Pathway: ask whether medication could be the cause; Oxfordshire guidance advises considering anxiety or depression

sentence: The NHS Every Mind Matters pages say a regular sleep routine can make it easier to fall asleep, because going to bed and getting up at similar times each day helps the body know when it is time to sleep.
note: Every Mind Matters: regular routine easier to fall asleep; similar times each day helps body know

sentence: They suggest keeping the same routine on days off.
note: Every Mind Matters: keep schedule on days off

sentence: They also suggest keeping phones, tablets and computers away for an hour before bed, because the light can delay sleep.
note: Every Mind Matters: avoid phones, tablets, computers for an hour before bed, light can delay sleep

sentence: Reading, meditation or breathing exercises are given as alternatives.
note: Every Mind Matters: reading, meditation, breathing exercises instead

sentence: A dark, quiet and cool bedroom is a recurring recommendation across NHS pages.
note: Keeping the room dark, quiet and cool recurring across NHS sites

sentence: NHS pages also advise against caffeine, smoking and alcohol in the hours before bed, although the exact timing differs from page to page.
note: One NHS page: avoid smoking, alcohol, tea and coffee for at least 6 hours; other pages give other times

sentence: Some pages advise against napping during the day and describe regular daytime exercise as helpful.
note: Summary of NHS tips: regular daytime exercise, avoid daytime naps

sentence: For someone who worries in bed, the NHS suggests writing a list of tasks for the next day before going to sleep.
note: Every Mind Matters: list things to do next day before sleeping

sentence: If a person is still awake after about 20 minutes, the NHS suggests getting up, doing something relaxing in another room, and going back to bed when sleepy.
note: Every Mind Matters/NHS guide: get up if awake after about 20 minutes, relax elsewhere, return when sleepy

sentence: The NHS suggests seeing a GP if changing sleeping habits has not helped insomnia, or if there has been trouble sleeping for months.
note: NHS insomnia: see a GP if habits have not helped or trouble sleeping for months

sentence: A GP may refer a person for cognitive behavioural therapy, or CBT, which helps change the thoughts and behaviours that get in the way of sleep.
note: NHS: GP may refer for CBT, which can help change thoughts and behaviours that keep you from sleeping

sentence: The NHS says GPs now rarely prescribe sleeping pills for insomnia, because they can have serious side effects and a person can become dependent on them.
note: NHS: GPs rarely prescribe sleeping pills; serious side effects and dependence

sentence: NHS sources describe cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia, known as CBT-I, as the main treatment for long-term insomnia.
note: UCLH clinic: most patients offered CBT-I first line; NHS Scotland guide describes it as the main treatment

sentence: A University College London Hospitals service says most patients with insomnia are offered a course of CBT-I first, and that waiting lists can apply.
note: UCLH: most patients offered CBT-I as first-line treatment, waiting lists can apply

sentence: A Scottish NHS self-help guide describes Sleepio as a free digital treatment that delivers a six-week CBT-I programme.
note: NHS inform/MoodJuice: Sleepio free digital six-week CBT-I programme

sentence: A primary care guideline from Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West advises that medicines are best avoided in the long-term management of insomnia.
note: BOB ICB guidance: pharmacological therapy should be avoided in long-term management of insomnia

sentence: NHS sources put the amount most adults need at about 7 to 9 hours a night.
note: Search summary: NHS sources put the figure at about 7 to 9 hours; NHS Scotland 7 to 9 hours for working-age adults

sentence: One NHS page says age, health and daily routine can all affect how much sleep a person needs.
note: One NHS page says age, health and daily routine can affect how much sleep you need

sentence: NHS Every Mind Matters says getting enough sleep can support mood, energy, the immune system and overall health.
note: Every Mind Matters: enough sleep supports mood, energy, immune system and overall health

sentence: A United States guide from the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute adds that regularly getting too little or very poor quality sleep increases the risk of high blood pressure, heart disease and other health problems.
note: NIH guide: not enough or very poor sleep regularly increases risk of high blood pressure, heart disease and other problems

sentence: NHS pages list feeling very tired, irritable or sleepy during the day among the signs of not sleeping enough.
note: Signs you may not be sleeping enough include feeling very tired, irritable or sleepy during the day

sentence: The NHS says a person may be referred to a sleep clinic if they have symptoms of another sleep disorder, such as sleep apnoea.
note: NHS insomnia page: may be referred to a sleep clinic if symptoms of another sleep disorder such as sleep apnoea

sentence: Fatigue, meaning overwhelming tiredness that rest and sleep do not relieve, may point to an underlying medical condition, according to NHS guidance linked to NHS Lothian.
note: Fatigue, an overwhelming tiredness not relieved by rest and sleep, may mean an underlying medical condition
